newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 8.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
COURT PULLS UP INVESTIGATING AGENCY CHIEF IN FODDER SCAM

The Central Bureau of India's (CBI) credibility in investigating the Bihar fodder scam took a knocking as Bihar High Court said CBI director Joginder Singh was interfering in the probe. It was alleged that the CBI chief had tried to delete the name of Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav from the list of those charged in the scam.
The Economic Times
DOMESTIC INDUSTRY TO BE PROTECTED

Industry Minister Murasoli Maran has declared that government's first duty would be to protect domestic industry. Now that government had achieved considerable progress in the foreign investment policy, the Industry Ministry planned to shift its focus to small-scale industry and the public sector, said Maran. The Minister's statement came in the wake of contrary signals being given by various ministries on economic policy and dissent raised against government's pro-foreign investment policy by domestic industry.
TATA SONS MAKES 2.99 BLN RUPEE RIGHTS ISSUE

Tata Group owned Tata Sons has made a 2.99 billion-rupee rights issue to several Tata Group companies. As a result, leading Tata companies had to shell out 300 million to 700 million rupees each to subscribe to the 1:5 rights issue. Shareholders of many group companies including Tata Chemicals, Tata Power and Telco were said to be unhappy with the move. The issue, made at 100,000 rupees per share, was picked up by Telco, Tata Chemicals, Tata Power, Indian Hotels, Tata Steel subsidiary Kalimati Investments and Bambino Investments & Trading Company.
Financial Express
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX DOWN 98 POINTS

Stocks continued to fall for a second day on Monday. Bombay and National Stock exchanges (BSE & NSE) saw their respective indices battered. The 30-share BSE sensitive index (Sensex) touched an intra-day low of 2,939 during mid-trading session, bounced back 62 points towards the end following profit taking by bears. The sensex finally closed at 3002.86, down 98.41 points from the previous closure. NSE-50 lost 30.12 points over the previous close of 904.12.
GDRS PLUNGE TO NEW LOWS

Prices of global depositary receipts (GDR) of Indian corporates plunged to new lows on Monday in tandem with the trends in the domestic market. The Skindia GDR Index touched a new low of 59.22 on October 4, down from an all-time low of 61.18 recorded on September 27. It had perked to a high of 90 on April 4,1996. The DSP GDR Index fell to new lows on Monday as it touched 70, down from previous low of 76.79 recorded a week ago. Early last month, DSP GDR stood at 88.34.
UNIT TRUST COLLECTIONS AT 12 BLN RUPEES

The Unit Trust of India (UTI) collected 12 billion rupees under various schemes offered by it during the first quarter ending September 1996. It sales target for the current financial year is pegged at 100 billion rupees. UTI's collection figures indicate the financial institution may not be able to meet its target during this fiscal. Given the poor market conditions, the going may get tougher for UTI, which is one of the reasons why UTI is concerned about its performance in the next three quarters.
Business Standard
GOVT TO PICK UP STAKE IN UNIT TRUST HOLDING FIRM

The Government, along with various state-run financial institutions, has decided to buy equity stakes in the proposed holding company of the Unit Trust of India (UTI). UTI is planning to restructure itself by forming a single holding company at the top. This company will, in turn, set up one asset management company to oversee funds management, which is UTI's current business, and also hold stakes in all UTI associate companies and subsidiaries.
INDUSTRIAL GROWTH DIPS TO 6.8 PCT

The industrial production in June 1996 grew by just 6.8 percent compared with 12.2 percent in the same period last year. The index of industrial production (base: 1980-81=100) showed the growth rate in the manufacturing sector slowed down to 9.1 percent in June as compared with 11.1 percent in June 1995. Electricity suffered a decline of 1.7 percent as compared with 14.6 percent. Mining saw a low growth of 2.0 percent as compared with 17.4 percent last year.
TRANSFER OF BASIC, CELLULAR LICENCES TO BE ALLOWED

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) is likely to allow assignability, or transfer, of both cellular and basic telecommunication licences. A decision to this effect was apparently taken by the Telecom Commission. The Commission plans to reduce the interconnect charges prescribed in the earlier agreement with operators by some 10 percent. It had earlier brought down port charges by 30 percent. DoT may also soften its earlier stance on other issues in the interconnect and licence agreements.
REGULATOR APPROVES IDBI DEBT ISSUE

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has approved the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI)'s proposed 10 billion debt issue. IDBI has been allowed to go ahead with the issue without appointing a monitoring institution to ensure the end-use of the issue proceeds. SEBI's clearance allowed IDBI to enter the capital market with the debt issue without creating a debenture redemption reserve.
The Observer
FOREIGN BANKS MAY FUND TELECOMMUNICATION LICENCEES

The US and European investment banks have shown interest in India's basic telecommunication (telecom) privatisation projects. Their representatives, present at the World Bank-IMF annual meeting, are reported to have given positive signals in this regard to the Indian representatives. US and European investment bankers apparently told the Indian representatives that India must allow control to foreign players in the telecom sector. They said the sector being capital and knowledge intensive could not be managed over a 15-year licence period without its control left in the hands of the foreign players.
Business Line
TRADE SURPLUS WITH U.S. DOWN TO $1.7 BLN

The share of the US in India's total trade has risen marginally from 13.2 percent during 1990-91 to 13.7 percent last year. This was despite booming bilateral trade which touched $9.4 billion in 1995/96 (April-March). India's exports to US grew by just 10 percent during the year compared to 26 percent in 1994-95. Even though India enjoyed a trade surplus with US, its exports to US shrank to $2.2 billion during 1994-95.
